title: Strict-system realization of an already normalized refinement
statement: Fix l, Omega, D, X,Y,f, compactifications c,d and a proper refinement r as in the refinement data. Given Transport records A,B and an already constructed Mates P for them, a finite coefficient field E, operations o on the strict E-system categories and a prescribed realization package R, there exists SystemRealization A B r P E o R. Its alpha inverse is the actual intrinsic proper/open refinement word before evaluation; its primitive proper/open/inverse-unit realizations and their termwise/Roos shifts give the prescribed integralMap equality with the integral left comparison in P. This is a lifting and realization statement for an existing normalized comparison; it does not construct any stage comparison or field descent map.

proof.text: On the strict semilinear systems put $\mathsf F^a=S_{p_a}J_{j_a}$ for $a=c,d$ and form $\mathsf C_u=c_{p_d,u}J_{j_c}\circ S_{p_d}\Gamma_{Q_u}:\mathsf F^d\to\mathsf F^c$, with $Q_u=(j_c,j_d,1_X,u)$. The system realization theorem constructs this map intrinsically, before evaluation, and identifies its evaluated maps with the normalized finite comparisons of step 1. On $\mathcal R_XK$ the input and both endpoints are normalized, have etale-origin constructible levels, and common cohomological/Tor bounds by integral reconstruction and system transport. Apply finite operations also to the open/proper intermediate morphisms, with their own compactifications, and take the larger of the finitely many common bounds. Since exact evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms, $\mathsf C_u$ is invertible on this domain. Define $\mathsf\alpha_u=\mathsf C_u^{-1}$. Only invertibility, never equality of maps, was detected by evaluations.

source.place: Section 5, Lemma 5.13, Construction 5.15; actual system operation model and evaluation.

proof.text:
Transport $\mathcal L_Y(\mathsf\alpha_u\mathcal R_X)$ through the specified identifications $F^a_R\cong\mathcal L_Y\mathsf F^a\mathcal R_X$ to define $\alpha_{u,R}$. Integral reconstruction supplies exactly those identifications and the prescribed $r_{a,R}$. The system-realization theorem intertwines $\Gamma_{Q_u}$ and direct-image composition with their ambient proper/open maps. It therefore gives, as an equality of actual integral transformations,
$$r_{d,R}\,I_Y(\alpha_{u,R})=(C_u^{\rm amb})^{-1}\,r_{c,R}.$$
Here $C_u^{\rm amb}$ is ambient proper composition after $Rp_{d,*}e_u$. Inversion and naturality preserve the intertwining equality. Its input system equality is the intrinsic proper/open word of step 2, not a family selected from finite components. This proves the integral normalization with the same compact-support representatives.

source.place: Construction 5.20 and normalized reduction/total-limit transport; blueprint exceptional inverse-image construction.

proof.text: The proper/open word commutes with shifts: its open base-change and clopen projection constituents do so on simultaneous complex models, and the direct-image shift is the adjoint of the termwise inverse-image shift. Units and counits commute with these adjoint shifts; writing a mate as unit, whiskered map and counit therefore preserves its shift square. The direct-image compositor is the conjugate of pullback composition, so the same argument applies to it. Composition, whiskering and inversion preserve shift compatibility. The constant ring sequence $C_m=A$ and evaluation give this argument at each finite coefficient; the diagram shift model imposes no normalization or constructibility assumption. For the integral maps, slotwise realization shift coherence identifies these same system shifts with the prescribed termwise/Roos-cone shifts under $r_{c,R},r_{d,R}$. Thus both left maps already constructed have the shifts required in the statement.
